key_insight: MedJev delivers competitive zero-shot medical predictions in a single forward pass on a laptop, but patient-level confidence estimates require local recalibration.
clinical_relevance: Low-cost local inference could support future clinical decision tools, although benchmark performance does not establish safety or effectiveness in practice.
method: Evaluated an open System One model that answers structured questions without generating text.
Compared zero-shot performance with LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models.
Tested two-parameter local recalibration using 50–200 labeled examples.
evidence_signal: Across 10 benchmarks, including MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-ED tasks, MedJev achieved 72.5% MedQA accuracy and 0.926 in-hospital mortality AUROC versus XGBoost’s 0.902.
watch_item: Patient-level predictions showed substantial miscalibration (mortality ECE 0.286, reduced to 0.007 after recalibration), and ED admission discrimination lagged supervised models.
paper_title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
